chunks: And it was narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, who said:
I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: A man divorced his wife and had two Nāṣibī witnesses testify.
He said: “Everyone who is born upon the fiṭrah and is known for righteousness in himself, his testimony is accepted.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاحِ: righteousness; recognized uprightness in personal conduct
key_terms.الْفِطْرَةِ: the natural disposition; innate primordial nature upon which one is born
key_terms.شَاهِدَيْنِ: two witnesses; the pair brought to testify
key_terms.شَهَادَتُهُ: his testimony; the legal witness statement under consideration
key_terms.طَلَّقَ: divorced; refers to the act of issuing divorce
key_terms.نَاصِبِيَّيْنِ: two Nāṣibīs; persons described as bearing enmity toward the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام

ai.seo_question: When is a witness’s testimony accepted in a divorce case according to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal acceptance of testimony in a divorce case. Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام states that testimony is accepted from one born upon the fiṭrah and known for personal righteousness, indicating a criterion centered on uprightness and apparent integrity.
